offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

tools.name: WebSearch
tools.description:
Search the web. Returns result blocks with titles and URLs. US-only.

- The current month is (provided in the conversation below) — use this when searching for recent information.
- `allowed_domains` / `blocked_domains` filter results.
- After answering from results, end with a "Sources:" list of the URLs you used as markdown links.

allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

blocked_domains.description: Never include search results from these domains

mode.description: "standard": the normal web search: quick and cheap; right for straightforward lookups (reference facts, official pages, documentation, well-known people, places and topics) and simple follow-up lookups. "extended": a thorough, fresh search at several times the cost and latency.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

I found no results describing Scion as a database for agent conversations. The results describe Scion as Anthropic's internal source control system, which is a different thing.

- **What it is:** Anthropic announced Scion on October 13, 2026, as an internal source control system that replaces Git for its main code repository. Anthropic says Scion "is by no means a suitable replacement for git for general use," will not be open-sourced, and suits only very large monorepos.
- **Why it was built:** Commit volume grew fast. One report says daily merges to the main branch went from about 2,500 in May 2026 to more than 30,000 in September 2026 (yage.ai, Chinese-language source).
- **How it stores data:** Per one account, Scion uses content hashes as storage addresses, so identical content is stored once. It also uses a three-tier cache (a host daemon, a regional cache, and a server backed by cloud storage). A 36Kr report says there is no fully materialized complete code repository in the entire system, nor on the server.
- **Team and effort:** One account says Anthropic assigned 7 engineers who spent 5 months writing Scion from scratch, and that effort also covered the code review tool Antique and code search.

On the "conversation database" angle, a third-party blog says Claude Code stores session history in a local SQLite file (`~/.claude/code/sessions.db`). That claim is unverified, and I'd treat it with caution. Nothing else in the results confirms an Anthropic conversation store, so if you need that, a search aimed at official Claude Code documentation would be more reliable.

I added both notes to the interactive-app Todo in `TODO.md`, and the anchor check passes.

**What I found on Scion.** Before your message I knew nothing about it, so I searched; everything here comes from reports, not from inside knowledge. Anthropic announced Scion on 2026-10-13 as an internal source-control system that replaces git for its monorepo. The driver was commit volume: one report says daily merges went from about 2,500 to over 30,000 between May and September 2026. Per the reports:
- **Storage:** content-addressed, with a three-tier cache.
- **Not open source:** it won't be released, and Anthropic calls it no general replacement for git.
- **Built with it:** a code-review tool, Antique, and code search.

I found nothing saying Scion links conversations to code. It reads as a scale answer to git: too many commits, too big a repo. Your guess about tighter coupling could still be right, since Antique would be the natural place for anchored comments. The Todo records it as your suspicion, not as fact.

One result claimed Claude Code stores sessions in a SQLite file. This workspace shows otherwise: the transcripts are the `.jsonl` files the agent-repo commits, so I left that out.

**The two notes:**
- **Try Delta before building:**
  - its link and beta dates
  - same goal, opposite means
  - what each side has that the other lacks
  - self-hosting unchecked
  - our lean that vc-x1 keeps the record and Delta, or our viewer, is a window onto it, decided by a trial on `t1`
  - the change-id-plus-line idea for anchored comments
- **Scion:** the facts above as reported, plus your suspicion, marked as not borne out by anything found.

Your earlier name for parallel cycles in the Todo **Scion and Parallel cycles** now collides with Anthropic's Scion. Do you want to rename it, or keep it?

content.content:
### agent-files(proposal): vc-x1 is the interface, jj the engine

(wink + agent, 2026-10-28) The rule **jj, not git** says version-control operations use jj, but in
a cycle the user does not and should not use jj. vc-x1 carries the model jj does not know, the
pair, the scope, the opening and closing, the trailers, and Land, with jj-lib as its engine.

- The rule becomes: in a cycle, version-control operations use vc-x1, and a reach for raw jj is a
  vc-x1 gap, filed as a Todo rather than written into the protocol as a workaround.
- Already said in parts: v0.3.1's **Warn rather than refuse** names raw jj as what "the tool exists
  to retire", and its re-describe rule retires `jj describe`. The bookmark moves by `jj git push`
  are what is left.
- Open: whether read-only jj, `jj log`, `jj st`, and `jj op log` for recovery, stays allowed as
  inspection and the escape hatch. The agent's suggestion is that it does.
- Its own proposal, after **agent-files(proposal): v0.3.1** (wink, 2026-10-28).

### Parallel cycles

(wink + agent, 2026-10-28) The model runs one cycle at a time, and the work must scale to several
changes at once, as Anthropic's Scion does for its agents. A design entry, its findings for a
`notes/` file.

- Sources: [Redesigning source
  control](https://www.anthropic.com/research/redesigning-source-control), [The Pulse on
  Scion](https://blog.pragmaticengineer.com/the-pulse-anthropic-builds-its-own-source-control-system/),
  and the prototypes [CarterT27/scion](https://github.com/CarterT27/scion) and
  [tinyhumansai/openscion](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openscion).
- What carries over from Scion:
  - making a change never touches a ref, and landing is a rebase onto the trunk as it is now and a
    compare-and-swap on the ref, retried, with no global lock
  - conflicts are expected and fixed after the merge, and humans review intent rather than every
    line
  - v0.3.1's `commit --closing` already merges onto the trunk as it is.
- What assumes one cycle, each a design point:
  - the working copy, one `@` per repo: a jj workspace per cycle, each on its bookmark
  - the record, one `## In Progress` and one `## Closed` in `TODO.md`: a record file per cycle
  - the version, bumped at each opening, so two cycles claim the same next one: assigned at Land
  - the agent-repo, one session's journal per `@` with trailers pairing commits: a workspace or a
    directory per session
  - the build and install, one `target/` and one `vc-x1-dev`: per workspace, a profile per cycle
  - the messages repo's single-clone mutex, its README's "No second machine": member-scoped ids.
- The human gates come first: per-push approval and the hard stop are what make the protocol
  trusted now, and the decision is which of them move to Land or to a review of a cycle's intent.
  We think the rest is mechanical.

input.prompt: Does Scion (or its review tool) store or link agent conversations/transcripts/intent with code changes, or anchor comments to code? Quote any sentences about conversations, transcripts, intent, review, comments, or a database. Also summarize its data model briefly.

toolu_01W4xSPYRYj8FBVkoDmighNU.prompt: Does Scion (or its review tool) store or link agent conversations/transcripts/intent with code changes, or anchor comments to code? Quote any sentences about conversations, transcripts, intent, review, comments, or a database. Also summarize its data model briefly.

content.content:
The page doesn't say Scion or Antique stores agent conversations, transcripts, or prompts, or links them to code changes. It also doesn't say comments are anchored to specific lines.

**Intent and review:** Reviewers look at a change's purpose rather than every line. The article says that "they now examine the _intent_ of the change as opposed to reading every line of code." The review tooling supports semantic approval rules: "the code review tooling we built can express complex semantic constraints on approvals." The only mention of comments is a passing reference to telling "comment-only changes" apart from sensitive logical changes.

**Database:** The page names Spanner as a backing store. Refs are updated with a "compare-and-swap on a single Spanner row," and derived data is written back to Spanner.

**Data model (brief):**
- **Changesets:** The unit of work is a changeset, an entry in a write-ahead log. It records the files changed relative to its first parent, "along with content-addressed pointers to the compressed file contents in blob storage."
- **Refs:** Branches and tags are discouraged, except for main and release branches.
- **Derived data:** Blame, path history, and commit-graph indices are computed from changesets, recursively from parent values, and are kept separate from the changeset itself.
- **Storage:** Content is content-addressed, and servers write results back to Spanner or cloud storage.

### lookup builds an index that correlates the two repos

(wink + agent, 2026-11-02) The hypothesis, wink's: with an index, one agent commit per cycle and one
per rung make no difference to correlating the two repos, so `lookup` builds the index in

content.text:
Yes. And `TODO.md` already decided what kind of database it is, in **lookup builds an index that correlates the two repos** (2026-11-02):
- **Derived:** it's "never the source of truth, so losing it costs only the rebuild".
- **Durable and rebuildable:** it lives in `tmp-durable/agent-repo-indexes/`, outside both repos.
- **Incremental and checked for staleness:** it records what it was built from, so a stale entry is rebuilt, never served.

So "an index" really means a database, but a cache, not a store. That's where vc-x1 differs from Delta, and it lines up with Scion:
- **Delta:** DeltaDB appears to be the source of truth for the conversations. Git holds only the code.
- **Scion:** changesets are the truth. Blame, path history and the commit-graph indices are "derived data", computed from the changesets and kept separate. That's our split exactly.
- **vc-x1:** the two git repos are the truth, and the database is derived from them. Delete it and rebuild, and nothing is lost. That's what keeps "plain git, any host, offline" true while still allowing a fast viewer.

**What I'd add when it's built:**
- **SQLite** as the engine, through `rusqlite`. It's one file, embedded, needs no server, and its FTS5 extension gives full-text search over transcripts. A rebuildable cache doesn't need anything bigger.
- **What it holds:**
  - both repos' commit graphs and the `ochid:` edges between them
  - transcript spans mapped to work commits, the existing Todo's core
  - the headings and anchors in `TODO.md` and `zTOC.md`, and rung titles matched to commits
- **Incremental updates** keyed by jj's operation id or commit ids, so each run only processes what changed.

**Where the pattern breaks: anchored comments.** A comment you write on a line is written by someone, not derived from anything, so it can't live in a cache that might be deleted. Keeping the principle means storing comments in git: in the agent-repo, or as a file in the work-repo keyed by change id plus line. The index then just reads them like everything else. That's the one design question that "we need a DB" actually raises.

The plain version: yes, it's a database, but a disposable one built from the git repos, the same split Scion uses. Only new authored data like anchored comments needs a real home, and that home should be git.

Should I add the SQLite choice, the contents, and the anchored-comments question to the lookup-index Todo?

Fair, I overstated it. "Disposable" describes where the first implementation starts, not a principle. If so, which data is the source of truth becomes a real design decision instead of a default. content.content:
### Improve init and add rename and delete subcommands

(wink + agent, 2026-10-11) A workspace's name is written into six places, and nothing renames or
removes them together: the work-repo's directory, the agent-repo's directory when it is not
nested, the two repos on the remote, each repo's `origin` URL, the `.vc-config.{toml|md}` of both
sides, and the Claude Code symlink. And `init` makes a workspace it cannot always finish, or that
Claude Code does not find.

- The order is wink's: `init` is fixed first, then `vc-x1 delete`, then `vc-x1 rename`. Each is a
  cycle of its own.
- The `init` work is more than one cycle, wink's order: the path over 200 characters, then the
  name GitHub would change, the order the two parts below are in. The first part, the agent
  template `--use-template` looked for, retired with the flag (2026-11-03).
- Delete is ahead of rename: its "find every part of a workspace from its config" is what rename
  reuses, and it gives `init` the cleanup it lacks.
- The parts are `####` headings, where [Todo format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format) asks for
  bullets with a bold title, since a heading is an anchor a link can name.
- Delete leans on two entries far down this list: the clean verdict of [status prints a verdict
  per repo and exits with a bit per
  side](#status-prints-a-verdict-per-repo-and-exits-with-a-bit-per-side), and [status reports the
  commits no bookmark reaches](#status-reports-the-commits-no-bookmark-reaches). Whether they move
  up ahead of it, or delete's cycle builds the verdict as its first rung, is open.
- One experiment wants wink starting a fresh Claude Code session, the symlink's below.

#### symlink names a path over 200 characters as Claude Code does

(2026-10-09) Claude Code cuts a project name longer than 200 characters to 200 and appends `-` and
a base-36 hash of the path, and `encode_path` returns the uncut name, so `vc-x1 symlink` makes a
link Claude Code never reads for such a path. Found in the installed Claude Code (2.1.295) during
the cycle "fix: symlink names a project as Claude Code does", which left it out: the hash function
has to be copied exactly, and no path met so far is near 200.

Whether the hash has to match bit for bit is not known, and the opening tests it before any code is
written. On a scratch project whose full path is over 200 characters, wink starting a fresh Claude
Code session there for each pass:
----
### init and clone take --custom

(wink + agent, 2026-10-17) With `custom.md` uncommitted, a fresh `init` or `clone` has none, and its
first session starts without the family's layer.

- `--custom <path>` copies the file at `<path>` into the new workspace as `custom.md`.
- We think a member's `custom.md` is mostly a pointer into the family's shared layer, so a copy
  rarely drifts, and an `update` subcommand that copies it again waits for a case that needs it.
- Follows the cycle **agent-files(proposal): v0.3.0**, which made `custom.md` optional.

----
### vc-x1 config and init write a simple config

(wink + agent, 2026-10-22) `vc-x1 config work` names the workspace's file and then prints the
schema, every key commented at its default or example, so it never shows what the file says, and
its form is the old TOML carrier's, `#` lines under bare `[table]` headers, which a `.vc-config.md`
cannot take without a fence around it. Each key is six lines, its doc, `used by`, `default`, its
reference url, the line itself, and a blank, 187 lines at 0.85.7-6, most of them `default:
(none)` and urls. `vc-x1 init` writes `[repos]` and `[remote]` and only the keys with a default,
commented, so a new workspace has no `[validate]`, `[build]`, or `[install]` to start from.
Found at the review of the rung **feat: vc-x1 install-dev puts the dev build on the PATH**, in
the cycle **feat: vc-x1 install stages, deploys, and runs builds**.

- The simple form is iiac-perf's `.vc-config.md`: a short intro, then per table one line of prose
  saying what it is for and a `toml` fence holding its values, no per-key bullets, defaults lines,
  or urls. The documentation stays in `vc-config.md`, where the schema keeps it.
- `vc-x1 config work` prints the workspace's config in effect in that form: the tables and the
----
### Every repo's .gitignore ignores .claude, and settings stay out of agent-repos

(wink + agent, 2026-10-21) The sandbox Claude Code runs commands in blocks writes to the project's
`.claude/settings.json`, `skills`, `hooks`, and more by mounting `/dev/null` over each, and for a
name that does not exist it first creates an empty read-only file on the host to mount over, seen
from outside as files that come and go during a sandboxed command. jj inside the sandbox skips
them as devices, but a `jj` run outside meanwhile, or after a sandboxed command died, would
snapshot them as new files. vc-x1 shows them since its work repo ignores only
`/.claude/settings.local.json`, narrowed when the agent-repo moved to `.agent-session`, where
`/.claude` had been ignored whole. `.agent-session/.claude` exists too, made by a session run from
inside the agent-repo, with `.cc-writes`.

The rule, wink's calls (2026-10-21):

- Every repo has a `.gitignore` with `/.claude`, the work repo, the agent-repo, a single repo.

### init defaults to --local

(wink, 2026-10-30) `vc-x1 init` makes the workspace on the machine and creates and publishes nothing
unless `--push` asks, as `commit` does in **Only push publishes**. Today it creates the remotes and
pushes, public on GitHub unless `--private`, so a bare `init` publishes a repo.

- `--push` is what creates the remotes and publishes, and the approval it needs is the rest of that
  section's. `--private` and `--push-retries` take effect with it.
- Publishing later needs a way: a workspace with no `origin` has nothing for `vc-x1 push` to push to,
  so `push`, or a command of its own, creates the remotes.
- The trailers: `init`'s cross-links then have no URL to stamp, so they take the path form **feat:
  ochid trailers are URLs** defines, `/.agent-session/<chid>`, and they stay valid after a remote
  appears, the URL being checked only on a URL form.
- The name: `--repo local` is already a category, a local directory of bare repos, which is a remote
  of a kind and not this `--local`, so one of the two is renamed or explained. `clone` is to be
  checked for the same default.
  - **feat: close, land, and push compose with testing** makes `init --test-repo <path>/<repo-name>`,
    with local bare remotes, so that name is not taken by `--local`. What a bare `init` does stays here.

----
### The run record misses workspace init

(agent, 2026-10-29) A `clone` run's first operation in each repo, jj-lib's `add workspace
'default'`, carries no run record, since it is made before vc-x1 opens a transaction. The record is
set at four places, `Session::start_tx` and the snapshot and the two git imports, and workspace
init is a fifth. Seen in a fresh `vc-x1-dev clone`, whose other three operations per repo carry
the run.

- Tag it, or treat the operation before a run's first as the run's base, which is what an undo
  restores to either way.
- `init` makes the same operation and is the other case to check.

----
### init adopt takes a git-only repo

(wink, 2026-09-21) **feat: init adopt takes a POR** took a jj repo colocated with git, with or
without a single-repo config, and points a git-only repo, `.git` with no `.jj`, at
`jj git init --colocate`, which the user runs before adopting. Adopt could run it: the facade's
colocated init creates a new `.git`, and attaching to an existing one is jj's other init path,
which the facade lacks.

### --repo takes a URL, and a separate flag takes the path for local remotes

(wink, 2026-09-21) `--repo local=<dir>` reads as the local work repo, where it names the directory
init creates the bare origins in, standing in for GitHub. The two categories of one flag also
overlap, since `remote=` takes a path prefix too, meaning bare repos someone else created. Split
them by what they take:

- `--repo <url>` names a remote on a server, a URL and never a path.
- A separate flag, `--repo-local <path>` or `--repo-test <path>`, the name for this cycle to settle,
  takes a path and only a path, and init creates the bare repos there. The two conflict.
- Init creates the path when it is missing. Today a missing one fails with jj's "Could not open
  data at", and only at the publish step, after an adopt has already committed the work repo, so
  preflight checks it before anything is written.
- The bares are named after the project, `<path>/<name>.git` and `<path>/<name>.agent-session.git`,
  not the fixed `remote-work.git`, so one path holds several projects' remotes as one GitHub account
  holds several repos. The fixtures and `tests/cli_sync.rs` are built on the fixed names.
- The user config's account keys, `repo.default` and `repo.category.<cat>`, were shaped for one
  flag with categories (0.41.1-4). Two flags want a key each, named by their long names, and the
  old keys rejected with a fix-it, which is work for [repos.agent becomes repos.agent-dir, and a
  command brings a config up to
  date](#reposagent-becomes-reposagent-dir-and-a-command-brings-a-config-up-to-date).
- `local=` and `remote=` as category values are rejected with a fix-it, not kept as aliases.

----
### vc-dr-apply.sh applies vc-x1's rules to a dual workspace

(wink + agent, 2026-11-03) `vc-x1 init` makes a bare dual workspace and stops: the two repos and
their remotes, on GitHub or local and bare with `--test-repo`, `.vc-config.md` with `[repos]` and
`[remote]`, the `~/.claude/projects` symlink, and the first commit. What goes in it is not vc-x1's
problem. A script fills it, `scripts/vc-dr-apply.sh [--from <vc-x1>] [--rev <rev>] [<workspace>]`,
written in the cycle of **agent-files(proposal): v0.3.1**, wink's call, and vc-x1 is its source, the
adopter whose rules a new repo starts from, its working copy's by default and `--landed` its
trunk's. The first use is the repo exploring the
io_uring interface.

- One script for both uses, since they differ only in the `init` before it, which the script never
  runs. A new project is `vc-x1 init --target foo`, then the script on `foo`. Converting an existing
  repo is `vc-x1 init --target . --adopt`, then the script on `.`.
- It lives in vc-x1, a tool shipped beside it and not part of the binary, and moves to a repo of its
  own if it grows or becomes an app. "Apply" names what it does to the workspace's files, and the
  `vc-dr-` prefix still reads once it is on the PATH.
- What a new repo takes, little of it copied:
  - Copied from vc-x1 at the commit: the set, `AGENTS.md` and `agent-data/`, and the generic files,
    `LICENSE-*` on both sides and the agent repo's `memory/MEMORY.md`.
  - Written from skeletons in the source's `scripts/vc-dr-apply-base/`, so they are reviewed
    like the rules: `TODO.md` in [Todo format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format), since vc-x1's holds
    its own records; `custom.md`, since vc-x1's is gitignored and local; and the agent repo's
    `README.md`, named for the new repo, since vc-x1's says `vc-x1.claude` and "bot repo".

Agreed on the meaning: `vc-x1 init --adopt` already converts an existing repo, and this cycle lets you do it with `--test-repo`, so the converted copy publishes only to local bare remotes. Looking through `## Todo` and the code, I'd combine it with one Todo and leave the rest.

**Combine: init adopt takes a git-only repo** (2026-09-21). Without it, your own acceptance check fails at its first step:
- `cargo init t1` makes a `.git` with no `.jj`.
- `--adopt` refuses that today and tells you to run `jj git init --colocate` first (`src/init/adopt.rs:98`).
- So "init an existing repo" really means "init an existing git repo". Making adopt colocate it itself is the same subject, small, and on the same code path.

**What the cycle does then:**
1. **`--adopt` accepts a git-only repo,** colocating it in place with its history untouched.
2. **`--test-repo` stops refusing `--adopt`.** Today `check_test_repo` lists `--adopt` among the flags it rejects (`src/init.rs:1256`).
3. **The `origin` question.** Today an adopted repo with an `origin` takes its remotes from it, and a GitHub `origin` means `gh repo create` for the agent side (`plan_existing_repo`, `src/init.rs:1782`). Under `--test-repo` that would publish. The two choices:
   - **Refuse it, my recommendation:** the error says to run `git remote remove origin` on the copy. It's explicit and changes nothing behind your back.
   - **Repoint it** at `REMOTES/<name>.git`. That's more convenient but silently changes the copy's `origin`.

**Leave separate, though related:**
- **--repo takes a URL, and a separate flag takes the path for local remotes.** `--test-repo` already did half of this (the named bare repos under one path). What's left is splitting `--repo local=`, which is its own cycle. Its "preflight before adopt commits anything" point does apply here, so I'd carry that one point into this cycle's checks.
- **init defaults to --local.** It's about what a bare `init` publishes, and it needs the path-form trailers. Bigger, and a different subject.
- **init and clone take --custom**, and **The run record misses workspace init.** Both are small but would be scope creep.
- **vc-dr-apply.sh applies vc-x1's rules to a dual workspace.** Not combined, but its "converting an existing repo" path becomes part of the acceptance check: run `vc-dr-apply.sh` on the adopted `t1`.

**A title that reads better:** `feat: init adopts a git repo, as a test repo too`. It's a single-step cycle, or two rungs if you'd rather review the git-only part first.

Shall I open it under that title, with refuse-the-`origin` as the plan?

content.text:
It's not quite a bug, but it does have a gap. `plan_existing_repo` (`src/init.rs:1782`) sorts an adopted repo's `origin` three ways:

| `origin` | What init does for the agent-repo |
|---|---|
| GitHub URL | `gh repo create`, then push |
| A path | creates a bare repo beside it, then push |
| Any other URL: GitLab, Gitea, Bitbucket, self-hosted | assumes the agent remote already exists (`ExternalPreExisting`) and pushes to it |

So GitLab is handled on purpose: vc-x1 can only create repos on GitHub, so for any other host the agent remote is yours to create first. Two things are wrong with how that plays out:

1. **It fails late.** For a URL, the preflight checks nothing; the code says "we can't preflight cheaply, let git push surface failures" (`src/init.rs:1402`). A missing agent remote is only found at the push, after adopt has already committed the work repo and created the agent-repo. You're left with a half-made workspace. A `git ls-remote <agent-url>` before anything is written would catch it, and it's cheap.
2. **GitLab may publish anyway.** GitLab's push-to-create makes a new private project on the first push. So "must exist already" can quietly become "created by the push", the same outcome as `gh repo create` but without saying so.

For this cycle, the test-repo check therefore has to work for any host. Under `--test-repo`, an adopted repo's `origin` is refused whenever it's a URL, any host, not only GitHub. A path `origin` is local but still someone else's bare repo, so I'd refuse that too: under `--test-repo` the remotes are REMOTES and nothing else.

Gap 1 is the same "preflight before adopt commits" point from **--repo takes a URL…**. It's small and on the same code path, so I'd fold it in: under `--adopt`, an `ExternalPreExisting` agent remote is checked with `ls-remote` before anything is written.

So the cycle, retitled to cover it: `feat: init adopts a git repo, as a test repo too`
1. `--adopt` accepts a git-only repo and colocates it.
2. `--test-repo` takes `--adopt`, and refuses any `origin`, URL or path, naming `git remote remove origin`.
3. `--adopt`'s preflight checks that an external agent remote exists before writing anything.

Shall I open it?

content.text:
You're right, and I was being too cautious. With `--test-repo` you've already said explicitly that the remotes go in REMOTES. Doing what you asked isn't changing anything behind your back, and nothing leaves the machine. So under `--test-repo`, an adopted clone gets its `origin` repointed, not refused:

- **The work repo:** `origin` becomes `REMOTES/<name>.git`, a new bare repo, and the clone's history is pushed there, so the test remote starts with the real history.
- **The agent-repo:** created at `REMOTES/<name>.agent-session.git`, as for any test repo.
- **The old GitHub URL** has two options:
  - keep it as `upstream`, so you can still fetch the real repo's new commits. vc-x1 only ever pushes to `origin`, and jj pushes to `upstream` only if you name it. This is my recommendation.
  - drop it entirely, for the strictest version of "nothing leaves".
- **The report says what it did:** "origin was github.com/…, now REMOTES/t1.git, the old one kept as upstream".

One implementation detail: the clone's remote-tracking bookmarks, such as `main@origin`, describe GitHub's positions. They must be forgotten before `origin` is repointed, or the first push to the empty bare repo is refused as stale. The push should also carry every local bookmark, not just `main`, so the test remote mirrors the clone.

**The cycle, revised:** `feat: init adopts a git repo, as a test repo too`
1. `--adopt` accepts a git-only repo and colocates it.
2. `--test-repo` takes `--adopt`. Any existing `origin`, URL or path, is repointed into REMOTES with the clone's history pushed there, and the old `origin` is kept as `upstream`.
3. `--adopt`'s preflight checks that an external agent remote exists before writing anything. That's the late-failure gap for GitLab and other hosts, without `--test-repo`.

**Acceptance check:**
- `cargo init t1` → adopt with `--test-repo` → `vc-dr-apply.sh` → a single-step cycle landed and pushed, all into `remotes/`
- the same on a GitHub clone, with GitHub untouched and `upstream` still fetchable

content.content:
## Waiting

Important work that cannot start yet. Each entry names what it waits on, in a form that can be
checked, and the rank it takes in `## Todo` once unblocked. Every opening checks each condition
and promotes what is met ([Opening](AGENTS.md#opening)).

- **Retire the frozen history: `notes/chores/` and `notes/done.md`.** (wink, 2026-08-27) They
  are frozen and no longer grow, and the agent-repo transcript plus git history hold what they
  hold. Delete both in one cycle, after a sweep turns every link into them (Todo entries, the
  backlog, rationale.md, the other members' messages) into a permalink at the SHA before the
  deletion.
  - Waits on: **`vc-x1 closed "<title>"`** landed, and the session viewer good enough to read
    a cycle's record from the transcript.
  - Place when unblocked: first.
- **Sync's remote look stops spawning git.** (wink + agent, 2026-10-09) Sync learns where a
  remote's bookmarks are by spawning `git ls-remote`, and downloads the commits of the ones that
  moved by spawning a `git fetch` that moves no ref, the sixth entry of the spawn register in
  `clippy.toml` and the one spawn of `git`. Replace `git_command` and its two callers in
  `src/jj/session.rs` with jj-lib's query, delete the `#[allow]`, and close the entry.
  - Waits on: jj-lib's public API offering that query. Neither 0.45.1 nor 0.46.0 has one:
    `rg -i 'ls.remote' src/` in the jj-lib source prints nothing, and its git subprocess layer is
    `pub(crate)`. An upstream feature request, once filed or found, is named here.
  - Place when unblocked: first, being one function.
- **lookup matches a line to its write by content.** (wink + agent, 2026-10-26) lookup resolves a
  line through blame to its commit and the commit's `ochid:` trailer to its agent partner, with
  the agent commits inside a time tolerance as candidates when there is no trailer. In one
  person's workspace the trailer is exact. In a shared repo it fails: a squash or rebase merge
  leaves blame on a commit no trailer names, and a trailer that survives may point into an
  agent-repo the reader cannot reach. Time fails too, many contributors' commits inside any
  tolerance.
  - The key that survives squash, rebase, and cherry-pick is the text: each transcript records
    what every Write and Edit put into a file, so a line is matched to the call that wrote it
    with no commit between. **dr1_every_committed_line_finds_its_transcript_write** checks a
    part of it. The layering: the trailer when it resolves, the content when it does not, time
    last.
  - What makes it hard: a line changed after the write, by a person or `cargo fmt`, needs a
    fuzzy match, a common line (`}`, `Ok(())`) needs its hunk for context, and every
    contributor's transcripts must be reachable and indexed, a privacy question as much as a
    technical one.
  - Waits on: **Cycles in a shared repo, by fork and pull request** opening, since the need
    arises there.
  - Place when unblocked: directly after it.

- `X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, ...: the commits between
- `X.Y.Z`: Close-out (bare version, no suffix)

**Preparation is optional.** A lightweight cycle, with no ladder and no setup commit, skips `-0` and
starts at `-1` (its first commit). A single-step cycle is one commit, the Close-out, and carries the
bare `X.Y.Z` ([Cycle shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)). The same holds at every level: a sub-cycle
needing no Preparation omits its `.0` (see Nesting). One that grows a Preparation later adds the `0`
step without renumbering siblings.

Disambiguation:

- `-10`: commit #10 (final identifier `10`), not a Preparation.
- `-1.0`: Preparation of the `-1` sub-cycle (final identifier `0`).

**Nesting.** Sub-cycles append another level, recursively:

- `X.Y.Z-3.0`: Preparation of the `-3` sub-cycle
- `X.Y.Z-3.1`, `X.Y.Z-3.2`: its commits between
- `X.Y.Z-3`: its Close-out
- `X.Y.Z-3.1.0`: Preparation of the `-3.1` sub-sub-cycle

Bump the version-of-record at the start of every step (the per-commit checklist carries the step),
so the manifest always records the commit it will be part of and, per the preference above, every
commit carries a distinct version.

## Agent-files version

The agent-files set has a version of its own, apart from the artifact's, so which set an adopter
carries is read from a listing rather than a diff, and an `agent-files` title has a token that is
unique by construction ([Project-declared types](prose.md#project-declared-types),
[why](rationale.md#agent-files-version)).

- **Record**: an empty file, `agent-data/agent-files-vX.Y.Z{-suffix}`, the version its name. `ls
  agent-data` shows it without a read, a bump is a rename, and
  `git log --diff-filter=A -- 'agent-data/agent-files-v*'` lists every version beside the commit

3697	## Closed
3698	
3699	The last cycle's finished record, moved here whole by its closing commit and deleted by the next
3700	opening ([Cycle-record](AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).
3701	
3702	### feat: test repos, vc-dr-apply, and the v0.3.1-(0,1,2) agent-files
3703	
3704	Renamed at its closing, wink's call (2026-11-04), from **feat: close, land, and push compose with
3705	testing**, the title the plan below carries to the next cycles: this cycle built what that plan
3706	needs, and its rungs from **feat: a test repo converts an existing repo** on were not started. The
3707	opening, published under the old title, was re-described to the new one with its trailers kept, a
3708	bend of **No re-describe without coordinating** on wink's go, and `trailers --update` refreshed the
3709	links after it.
3710	
3711	Filed and opened the same day, wink's call (2026-11-02), from the anomaly the closing of **feat:
3712	improve trailers** ran into. Folds in three Todos, moved here below.
3713	
3714	#### Problem
3715	
3716	(wink + agent, 2026-11-02) Closing a cycle should be obvious, and to the user's liking, and `vc-x1`
3717	should help them do it properly. It does not:
3718	
3719	- A local cycle's closing holds `ocid: .../xxxx` until `vc-x1 land` commits the agent `@`, and that
3720	  rewrites all of the cycle's commits, 12 last time, so what was tested is not by SHA what lands.
3721	- The way through took five steps, which wink called a non-starter, and the one-command answer
3722	  gives up the test pause.
3723	- `land` needs the agent repo, so a work-only land, a merge or rebase, or a share for others to test
3724	  drags in a permanent link it does not need.
3725	- Nothing says where a cycle stands or what may come next.
3726	- The commands are already separate, so that is not the problem, wink's (2026-11-02). They do not
3727	  compose: the user wants to test between any two of them, passively by `validate`, and actively by
3728	  you, me, and others running a build named by `profile.<name>.suffix`. Today that is by hand and on
3729	  the real repos, and full `validate` runs `cargo fmt`, which can dirty the `@` the next step needs
3730	  empty.
3731	
3732	#### The Todos it folds
3733	
3734	##### commit --closing reads the nearest opening's title
3735	
3736	(wink 2026-11-1: this these 2 `commit --closing` should be one cycle?)
3737	
3738	(wink + agent, 2026-10-26) Without `--title`, `commit --closing` takes the cycle title from the
3739	opening above the trunk, and with cycles stacked on one line it reads the oldest: the closing of
3740	**feat: vc-x1 land** came out as **feat: vc-x1 commit takes a revision closing**, the stack's first
3741	cycle, and was made with `--title`.
3742	
3743	- The opening read is the nearest below the tip, the cycle's own, so a stack closes its top cycle.
3744	- A test closes a stack of two cycles without `--title`.
3745	
3746	##### commit --closing merges onto the cycle's base when it was opened above the trunk
3747	
3748	(wink 2026-11-1: this seem convient, but not sure the why,when,downsides,dangers)
3749	
3750	(wink + agent, 2026-10-26) `commit --closing` merges the trunk with the tip, so a cycle opened
3751	above the trunk, on an unlanded series as **feat: vc-x1 land** was, gets a closing whose first
3752	parent is the trunk, and the cycles below it leave `main`'s first parents for the second parent's
3753	ladder. That closing was re-parented by hand onto the fix commit its opening sat on.
3754	
3755	- The first parent is the opening's parent, where the cycle's bookmark was created, when that
3756	  descends from the trunk, and the trunk otherwise, so `git log --first-parent` reads one commit
3757	  per cycle.
3758	- A test closes a cycle opened above an unlanded one and checks both parents.
3759	
3760	##### land lands @- by default
3761	
3762	(wink + agent, 2026-10-29) `land`'s `--source` defaults to "the one local bookmark besides
3763	`--onto`", which depends on every bookmark in the repo and fails once there are two. The rest of
3764	vc-x1 works from the line's `@-`, `push` moving its bookmark there and `commit --closing` naming it.
3765	
3766	- `--source` left out is `@-`, with the work `@` empty: what lands is then the tree validation ran
3767	  on, and nothing uncommitted is left behind. `commit --closing` without `--land` leaves exactly
3768	  this, the closing at `@-` and an empty `@`.
3769	- A non-empty work `@` is refused, naming `--source`, rather than warned about, since a land is
3770	  pushed and permanent on the trunk. A merge `@`, whose `@-` is ambiguous, is refused too.
3771	- The empty check is the work-repo's alone: the agent `@` holds the session and is never empty.
3772	- An explicit `--source` lands what it names, with no check of `@`.
3773	- The cycle's bookmark is found from `@-` as today: its own, else its nearest parent's above
3774	  `--onto`, several refused with the list.
3775	- The help: `--source <BM|REV>`, "The cycle's last commit, a bookmark or a revision [default: @-,
3776	  with @ empty]".
3777	
3778	#### Solution
3779	
3780	Done in this cycle: `init --test-repo` makes a test repo, and `init --use-template` goes; `commit -s
3781	a --covers` makes the agent commit a cycle's rungs share; `scripts/vc-dr-apply.sh` applies a
3782	source's rules to a bare workspace, from its working copy by default, with language skeletons by
3783	`--lang`; the cycle-record is `TODO.md`'s again, `zTOC.md` holding the one ladder; and the
3784	agent-files are the drafts `v0.3.1-0` to `v0.3.1-2`. What follows is the plan as it stood, carried
3785	to the next cycles.
3786	
3787	Provisional. Three steps, each doing one thing, that compose with testing:
3788	
3789	- Every step leaves a state that can be tested, nothing half-done.
3790	- A step may repeat, so the user can test, tweak, and close again.
3791	- Testing does not disturb the cycle or block the next step.
3792	- Each tester's binary says what it is, its suffix the build and its version the commit.
3793	- Exit codes can be trusted, so the steps and the tests chain in a plain shell, and `vc-x1` does not
3794	  run the tests itself.
3795	
3796	The steps:
3797	
3798	- close makes the cycle's final shape, single-step or a trapezoid, local, with `--scope` defaulting to
3799	  work. It may be run again, and the agent and the user keep iterating on it.
3800	- land merges or fast-forwards onto any bookmark, local, and it may repeat. `--scope` defaults to work,
3801	  and it takes any scope that applies.
3802	- push to any other bookmark shares the work for backup or testing, with `xxxx` still in it. Push to a
3803	  release bookmark with `-s b` seals: it commits the agent `@`, fills the `ocid:`, refreshes any stale
3804	  `pcid:`, checks each tree unchanged, and publishes the agent repo first.
3805	- A release bookmark is one the user treats as permanent: `[release] bookmarks`, or `main` and `master`
3806	  when that key is absent. Work alone with an unsealed agent commit is an error there, unless `--yes`.
3807	
3808	The links follow one general rule, for any mix of work and agent commits:
3809	
3810	- `ochid:` is one line per related commit, on either side.
3811	- Every `ocid:` is the SHA of an agent commit the same commit's `ochid:` lines name, matched by
3812	  resolving it and not by line order.
3813	- A work commit's `ocid:` is real only when its agent commit was made before it, wink's (2026-11-02),
3814	  and otherwise stays `xxxx`. So most are `xxxx`, rungs included and on a release bookmark, and are
3815	  never rewritten. In an N:1 cycle only the closing has a real one, the seal committing the
3816	  agent repo before
3817	  the closing's final form. In 1:1 pairs every commit has a real one.
3818	- Each agent commit's SHA is carried by exactly one work commit, the last it names.
3819	
3820	#### Acceptance check
3821	
3822	This cycle's, pass: a test repo made by `init --test-repo`, with `vc-dr-apply.sh --lang` applied
3823	from vc-x1's working copy, validates from its first commit, run for every language in **feat:
3824	vc-dr-apply takes the active version and offers language skeletons**. The check below is the plan's,
3825	carried with it and not run here.
3826	
3827	By `vc-x1-dev`, on repos made by `init --test-repo <path>/<repo-name>`, in a table-driven test:
3828	
3829	- An N:1 cycle: close leaves every `ocid:` at `xxxx`. A tweak and a second close work. `land` with no
3830	  `--scope` leaves the agent repo alone, and a push to any other bookmark keeps `xxxx`, at any scope.
3831	- A push to a release bookmark with `-s b` commits the agent `@`, fills only the closing's `ocid:`,
3832	  leaves every rung's `xxxx` and SHA unchanged and the closing's tree identical, and pushes the agent
3833	  repo first. Pushed to a second release bookmark, the commits are already sealed and nothing changes.
3834	- A push to a release bookmark of work alone, with an agent commit no commit carries the SHA of, is an
3835	  error naming `-s b` and `--yes`, and with `--yes` it publishes and warns. An unsealed closing naming
3836	  another agent `@` is refused, and a release bookmark that moved is refused before anything is
3837	  committed.
3838	- The release bookmarks: with no key, `main` and `master`, so an old config works, and with `[release]
3839	  bookmarks`, that list alone, a project's `main` then being an ordinary bookmark.
3840	- A test between any two steps, `validate` or a suffixed build, changes nothing the next step depends
3841	  on, and the next step runs.
3842	- Two clones of one local remote give a moved trunk and another's commits, with no network.
3843	- 1:1 pairs carry a real `ocid:` on every commit and never `xxxx`.
3844	- `validate-desc` and `lookup` accept 1:1, N:1, 1:M, N:M, and mixed, and this repo's `main`, where every
3845	  rung of **feat: improve trailers** carries an `ocid:`, reports what it reports today.
3846	- close, land, and push each end by printing where the cycle stands and what may come next.
3847	- `vc-x1 validate` passes.
3848	
3849	#### Deliberation
3850	
3851	- Close makes no agent commit, wink's (2026-11-02), reversing the agent's proposal: the agent and the
3852	  user iterate after close, the conversation belongs in the cycle's own agent commit, and rework stays
3853	  free since nothing on the agent side names a rung yet.
3854	- The seal is the push to a release bookmark, wink's (2026-11-02), reversing the agent's land-as-seal:
3855	  land may
3856	  be a merge or a rebase on any bookmark, and sharing to test needs no permanent link. Only the release
3857	  line is permanent.
3858	  - The cost: no test at the final SHA before the release, only at an identical tree, and the binary's
3859	    embedded SHA differs. A tester's SHA for the closing never reaches `main`, the rungs' do.
3860	  - It bends **Only push publishes**, one push rewriting before it publishes, so it says so plainly and
3861	    `--dry-run` shows every rewrite.
3862	  - We think sealing is callable on its own too, since a pull request's merge is GitHub's and runs no
3863	    `vc-x1 push`. It is built as a step of its own, whether or not it gets a flag now.
3864	- `ocid:` is real only when the agent commit came first, wink's (2026-11-02), so a rung's stays `xxxx`
3865	  rather than being absent or rewritten, and the commit that carries an agent commit's SHA is the last
3866	  it names, wink's and the agent's, generalizing closing-only. A reader goes from a rung to its agent
3867	  commit by `ochid:`. Wink's "next commit" is the fallback once the last is on the release line, a
3868	  one-way link. Rejected as the norm: on a closing, "next" is the next cycle's opening, so
3869	  `main`'s landmark
3870	  would have no link to its conversation.
3871	- Any mix is valid, wink's (2026-11-02): N:M, so readers and validators accept all of it and stop
3872	  requiring links to be mutual. Writers stay at 1:1 and N:1 here, as **commit writes every mix of work
3873	  and agent commits** files, and the agent's mid-cycle commit is **An agent commit mid-cycle backs up
3874	  the transcript**.
3875	- A test repo is `init --test-repo <path>/<repo-name>`, wink's (2026-11-02), with no config key: each
3876	  is a path to `cd` into or name by `-R`, so there may be several.
3877	  - It is local, and makes local bare remotes, as `--repo local=<parent>` does, since testing `push`
3878	    needs a remote.
3879	  - `--local` is the default rather than a flag to reach for, wink's (2026-11-02), so the name says what

## Closed

The last cycle's finished record, moved here whole by its closing commit and deleted by the next
opening ([Cycle-record](AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).

### feat: test repos, vc-dr-apply, and the v0.3.1-(0,1,2) agent-files

Renamed at its closing, wink's call (2026-11-04), from **feat: close, land, and push compose with
testing**, the title the plan below carries to the next cycles: this cycle built what that plan
needs, and its rungs from **feat: a test repo converts an existing repo** on were not started. The
opening, published under the old title, was re-described to the new one with its trailers kept, a
bend of **No re-describe without coordinating** on wink's go, and `trailers --update` refreshed the
links after it.

Filed and opened the same day, wink's call (2026-11-02), from the anomaly the closing of **feat:
improve trailers** ran into. Folds in three Todos, moved here below.

#### Problem

(wink + agent, 2026-11-02) Closing a cycle should be obvious, and to the user's liking, and `vc-x1`
should help them do it properly. It does not:

- A local cycle's closing holds `ocid: .../xxxx` until `vc-x1 land` commits the agent `@`, and that
  rewrites all of the cycle's commits, 12 last time, so what was tested is not by SHA what lands.
- The way through took five steps, which wink called a non-starter, and the one-command answer
  gives up the test pause.
- `land` needs the agent repo, so a work-only land, a merge or rebase, or a share for others to test
  drags in a permanent link it does not need.
- Nothing says where a cycle stands or what may come next.
- The commands are already separate, so that is not the problem, wink's (2026-11-02). They do not
  compose: the user wants to test between any two of them, passively by `validate`, and actively by
  you, me, and others running a build named by `profile.<name>.suffix`. Today that is by hand and on
  the real repos, and full `validate` runs `cargo fmt`, which can dirty the `@` the next step needs
  empty.

#### The Todos it folds

##### commit --closing reads the nearest opening's title

(wink 2026-11-1: this these 2 `commit --closing` should be one cycle?)

(wink + agent, 2026-10-26) Without `--title`, `commit --closing` takes the cycle title from the
opening above the trunk, and with cycles stacked on one line it reads the oldest: the closing of
**feat: vc-x1 land** came out as **feat: vc-x1 commit takes a revision closing**, the stack's first
cycle, and was made with `--title`.

- The opening read is the nearest below the tip, the cycle's own, so a stack closes its top cycle.
- A test closes a stack of two cycles without `--title`.

##### commit --closing merges onto the cycle's base when it was opened above the trunk

(wink 2026-11-1: this seem convient, but not sure the why,when,downsides,dangers)

(wink + agent, 2026-10-26) `commit --closing` merges the trunk with the tip, so a cycle opened
above the trunk, on an unlanded series as **feat: vc-x1 land** was, gets a closing whose first
parent is the trunk, and the cycles below it leave `main`'s first parents for the second parent's
ladder. That closing was re-parented by hand onto the fix commit its opening sat on.

- The first parent is the opening's parent, where the cycle's bookmark was created, when that
  descends from the trunk, and the trunk otherwise, so `git log --first-parent` reads one commit
  per cycle.
- A test closes a cycle opened above an unlanded one and checks both parents.

##### land lands @- by default

(wink + agent, 2026-10-29) `land`'s `--source` defaults to "the one local bookmark besides
`--onto`", which depends on every bookmark in the repo and fails once there are two. The rest of
vc-x1 works from the line's `@-`, `push` moving its bookmark there and `commit --closing` naming it.

- `--source` left out is `@-`, with the work `@` empty: what lands is then the tree validation ran
  on, and nothing uncommitted is left behind. `commit --closing` without `--land` leaves exactly
  this, the closing at `@-` and an empty `@`.
- A non-empty work `@` is refused, naming `--source`, rather than warned about, since a land is
  pushed and permanent on the trunk. A merge `@`, whose `@-` is ambiguous, is refused too.
- The empty check is the work-repo's alone: the agent `@` holds the session and is never empty.
- An explicit `--source` lands what it names, with no check of `@`.
- The cycle's bookmark is found from `@-` as today: its own, else its nearest parent's above
  `--onto`, several refused with the list.
- The help: `--source <BM|REV>`, "The cycle's last commit, a bookmark or a revision [default: @-,
  with @ empty]".

#### Solution

Done in this cycle: `init --test-repo` makes a test repo, and `init --use-template` goes; `commit -s
a --covers` makes the agent commit a cycle's rungs share; `scripts/vc-dr-apply.sh` applies a
source's rules to a bare workspace, from its working copy by default, with language skeletons by
`--lang`; the cycle-record is `TODO.md`'s again, `zTOC.md` holding the one ladder; and the
agent-files are the drafts `v0.3.1-0` to `v0.3.1-2`. What follows is the plan as it stood, carried
to the next cycles.

Provisional. Three steps, each doing one thing, that compose with testing:

- Every step leaves a state that can be tested, nothing half-done.
- A step may repeat, so the user can test, tweak, and close again.
- Testing does not disturb the cycle or block the next step.
- Each tester's binary says what it is, its suffix the build and its version the commit.
- Exit codes can be trusted, so the steps and the tests chain in a plain shell, and `vc-x1` does not
  run the tests itself.

The steps:

- close makes the cycle's final shape, single-step or a trapezoid, local, with `--scope` defaulting to
  work. It may be run again, and the agent and the user keep iterating on it.
- land merges or fast-forwards onto any bookmark, local, and it may repeat. `--scope` defaults to work,
  and it takes any scope that applies.
- push to any other bookmark shares the work for backup or testing, with `xxxx` still in it. Push to a
  release bookmark with `-s b` seals: it commits the agent `@`, fills the `ocid:`, refreshes any stale
  `pcid:`, checks each tree unchanged, and publishes the agent repo first.
- A release bookmark is one the user treats as permanent: `[release] bookmarks`, or `main` and `master`
  when that key is absent. Work alone with an unsealed agent commit is an error there, unless `--yes`.

The links follow one general rule, for any mix of work and agent commits:

- `ochid:` is one line per related commit, on either side.
- Every `ocid:` is the SHA of an agent commit the same commit's `ochid:` lines name, matched by
  resolving it and not by line order.
- A work commit's `ocid:` is real only when its agent commit was made before it, wink's (2026-11-02),
  and otherwise stays `xxxx`. So most are `xxxx`, rungs included and on a release bookmark, and are
  never rewritten. In an N:1 cycle only the closing has a real one, the seal committing the
  agent repo before
  the closing's final form. In 1:1 pairs every commit has a real one.
- Each agent commit's SHA is carried by exactly one work commit, the last it names.

#### Acceptance check

This cycle's, pass: a test repo made by `init --test-repo`, with `vc-dr-apply.sh --lang` applied
from vc-x1's working copy, validates from its first commit, run for every language in **feat:
vc-dr-apply takes the active version and offers language skeletons**. The check below is the plan's,
carried with it and not run here.

By `vc-x1-dev`, on repos made by `init --test-repo <path>/<repo-name>`, in a table-driven test:

- An N:1 cycle: close leaves every `ocid:` at `xxxx`. A tweak and a second close work. `land` with no
  `--scope` leaves the agent repo alone, and a push to any other bookmark keeps `xxxx`, at any scope.
- A push to a release bookmark with `-s b` commits the agent `@`, fills only the closing's `ocid:`,
  leaves every rung's `xxxx` and SHA unchanged and the closing's tree identical, and pushes the agent
  repo first. Pushed to a second release bookmark, the commits are already sealed and nothing changes.
- A push to a release bookmark of work alone, with an agent commit no commit carries the SHA of, is an
  error naming `-s b` and `--yes`, and with `--yes` it publishes and warns. An unsealed closing naming
  another agent `@` is refused, and a release bookmark that moved is refused before anything is
  committed.
- The release bookmarks: with no key, `main` and `master`, so an old config works, and with `[release]
  bookmarks`, that list alone, a project's `main` then being an ordinary bookmark.
- A test between any two steps, `validate` or a suffixed build, changes nothing the next step depends
  on, and the next step runs.
- Two clones of one local remote give a moved trunk and another's commits, with no network.
- 1:1 pairs carry a real `ocid:` on every commit and never `xxxx`.
- `validate-desc` and `lookup` accept 1:1, N:1, 1:M, N:M, and mixed, and this repo's `main`, where every
  rung of **feat: improve trailers** carries an `ocid:`, reports what it reports today.
- close, land, and push each end by printing where the cycle stands and what may come next.
- `vc-x1 validate` passes.

#### Deliberation

- Close makes no agent commit, wink's (2026-11-02), reversing the agent's proposal: the agent and the
  user iterate after close, the conversation belongs in the cycle's own agent commit, and rework stays
  free since nothing on the agent side names a rung yet.
- The seal is the push to a release bookmark, wink's (2026-11-02), reversing the agent's land-as-seal:
  land may
  be a merge or a rebase on any bookmark, and sharing to test needs no permanent link. Only the release
  line is permanent.
  - The cost: no test at the final SHA before the release, only at an identical tree, and the binary's
    embedded SHA differs. A tester's SHA for the closing never reaches `main`, the rungs' do.
  - It bends **Only push publishes**, one push rewriting before it publishes, so it says so plainly and
    `--dry-run` shows every rewrite.
  - We think sealing is callable on its own too, since a pull request's merge is GitHub's and runs no
    `vc-x1 push`. It is built as a step of its own, whether or not it gets a flag now.
- `ocid:` is real only when the agent commit came first, wink's (2026-11-02), so a rung's stays `xxxx`
  rather than being absent or rewritten, and the commit that carries an agent commit's SHA is the last
  it names, wink's and the agent's, generalizing closing-only. A reader goes from a rung to its agent
  commit by `ochid:`. Wink's "next commit" is the fallback once the last is on the release line, a
  one-way link. Rejected as the norm: on a closing, "next" is the next cycle's opening, so
  `main`'s landmark
  would have no link to its conversation.
- Any mix is valid, wink's (2026-11-02): N:M, so readers and validators accept all of it and stop
  requiring links to be mutual. Writers stay at 1:1 and N:1 here, as **commit writes every mix of work
  and agent commits** files, and the agent's mid-cycle commit is **An agent commit mid-cycle backs up
  the transcript**.
- A test repo is `init --test-repo <path>/<repo-name>`, wink's (2026-11-02), with no config key: each
  is a path to `cd` into or name by `-R`, so there may be several.
  - It is local, and makes local bare remotes, as `--repo local=<parent>` does, since testing `push`
    needs a remote.
  - `--local` is the default rather than a flag to reach for, wink's (2026-11-02), so the name says what
    the repo is for, and what a bare `init` does stays with **init defaults to --local**.
- `--scope` defaults to work, always, wink's (2026-11-02), and any scope that applies may be named.
  - It reverses **commit works at every scope, and --local keeps it on the machine**'s `--land` requiring
    `--scope`, since a work-only land moves no agent commit.
  - This cycle does it for close, land, and push, and the rest of the commands stay with that entry.
- The tests run outside `vc-x1`, wink's and the agent's (2026-11-02): composing is the steps' job and a
  shell's, and `validate takes any profile` stays its own Todo.
- The agent repo may have branches someday, merged at a final Land, wink's heads-up (2026-11-02), so
  nothing here assumes the agent repo is linear, and the readers rely on the trailers alone.
- `xxxx` is an error only on a release bookmark, wink's (2026-11-02): it is fine on a test branch and
  probably a mistake on `main`, so the user defines the set, with `main` and `master` hard-coded for
  existing configs.
  - The key is `[release] bookmarks`, the agent's: a property of the repo and not a cycle, and the rules
    say bookmark. `[cycle] trunk` stays, where a cycle lands by default and not what is protected.
  - A key that is present replaces the two names rather than adding to them, the agent's: otherwise a
    project developing on `main` and releasing on `stable` could never take `main` off.
  - The check is per agent commit, the agent's: rungs keep `xxxx`, so a search for it would refuse every
    push. Each group of commits naming one agent commit needs one real `ocid:`.
  - Other commands read the same set, `trailers --update`'s refusal first, which names the trunk today.
  - `--yes` is no human check, an agent typing it as easily, so the agent passes it only when wink says
    so for that push. **Only push publishes** has the mechanism as open.
  - It catches a mistake made through `vc-x1` and no more: a raw `jj git push` or a pull request's merge
    goes around it, and branch protection is the tool for that.
- `vc-x1 close` is a subcommand, the agent's, to confirm: it pairs with `land` and `push`, and `commit
  --closing` shares its code.
- This cycle is local and work-only until its Land, per the v0.3.1 prototype `custom.md` names:
  - every commit is `commit -s w --no-push`, the opening with `--skip remote` too, bending Opening step
    2 and the per-rung flow's push. The description review goes and the work review stays. The Land is
    outside the bend, its pushes approved as usual.
  - commits and the Land run by `vc-x1-dev`, as `zDOING.md`'s Rule said, now `versioning.md`'s
    **Which build runs**.

#### Rungs

The rung subsections, in the ladder's order. The ladder itself, each rung with its marker, is
[zTOC.md](zTOC.md#ladder).

## The In Progress block

A cycle's record, `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, written at the opening
([Opening](../AGENTS.md#opening)), finalized and moved to `## Closed` by the closing commit, and
deleted by the next opening ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)). The picked-up `## Todo`
item is moved here (never copied) and becomes the cycle-record's **provisional items**, all
required, all revised as rungs land. The title is a heading one level below `## In Progress` and the
other five are headings one level below the title (a plain cycle: `###` title, `####` items, and
under a program heading, each one deeper):

- **title**, the cycle's name, what `git log --grep` finds it by
- **problem statement**: what is wrong, a sentence or two
- **solution statement**: what will be done about it, broad. Provisional, and the close-out's commit
  body carries the final one
- **acceptance check**: the measure of "are you finished?", specific enough that a reader can run
  it. Not the per-commit validation, which asks whether the artifact still works. A changed check is
  one of the things the deliberation exists to justify
- **deliberation**: how the other five were decided, one bullet per decision. The bullet's lead
  names the decision and its sentence states it, and the sub-bullets carry the reasons, the
  alternatives weighed, and the costs accepted, so a reader can skim the decisions and read the
  reasons only where they doubt one. `_None._` when there was nothing to deliberate, which is a real
  answer
- **rungs**: a `#### Rungs` heading over the rung subsections, the ladder itself being `zTOC.md`'s
  ([zTOC format](#ztoc-format)): one rung per step, `- 2 (done) [<title>](TODO.md#<slug>)`: the
  rung's version suffix, which `-V` and the installed dev build print, then the marker, `(done)` or
  `(current)`, both first so they read down their columns, and a rung not yet started has neither,
  its suffix being set when its commit bumps the version, and an inline link so the ladder is one
  list with nothing beside it to keep in step, its line as long as the title makes it. `<title>` is
  the rung's commit title, `<type>: <desc>` per [Conventional-commit
  shape](prose.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit), so a moved `## Todo` entry is retitled.
  The closing rung, `<cycle title> closing`, is linked like the rest

`#### Rungs` holds the **rung subsections**, one per rung in the ladder's order, the closing
included, headed by the rung's exact title, so the ladder is their index. Each opens at laddering
with an abstract-sized intent statement (the rung's problem and solution in a sentence or two) and
completes at the rung's landing with the conceptual delta: design points, consequences, deferrals,
never a restatement of the landed commit body. The closing rung's opens with the stub "Closing out
the cycle." and completes at close-out with what closing taught, in problem/solution form, or
`_None._`.

A rung is `- N (marker) [<title>](TODO.md#<slug>)` and carries no detail beyond that: the title
links to the rung's subsection. A step is identified by its title (prose.md's [Steps are named, not
numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)), so a title carries no number, no version, and no
SHA. The version-of-record still bumps for every rung and its suffix still encodes the stage, but
that encoding belongs to the manifest and appears nowhere in prose.

A single-step cycle's ladder is one unlinked rung, `- N (marker) <cycle title>`, with no subsection
under it: a subsection headed by the title would collide with the title heading's anchor ([Cycle
shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).

The block is the cycle's only record. A design finding that must outlive the cycle goes into a
`notes/` file by the rung that made it ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).

# Cycle model

A cycle's `## In Progress` block, shown as a specimen rather than a skeleton: the `config loader`
cycle, mid-run, with its opening landed and its first work rung current. Copy the shape, not the
words. The rules are in [The In Progress block](notes.md#the-in-progress-block).

One thing the specimen cannot show:

- a single-step cycle drops both bookends and all the steps are in the one commit: the ladder is one
  unlinked rung with the bare title, and there are no rung subsections under it ([Cycle
  shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).

## In Progress

### refactor: extract config loader

#### Problem

Config parsing lives inside the CLI entry point, so every subcommand that wants a setting reaches
through `main` for it, and a test cannot load a config without building the CLI.

#### Solution

Move config loading into its own module with a single `load` entry point that the CLI and the tests
call alike.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with a new test that loads a config from a fixture file without touching `main`,
and `vc-x1 config --validate` reports the same findings as before the move.

#### Deliberation

- one work rung, not two: the parser and the loader were going to be split first and moved second,
  but the move is what forces the split, so doing them together is fewer edits
- the acceptance check compares `config --validate` output rather than asserting on internals, so a
  later rename inside the module does not invalidate it

#### Rungs

The rung subsections, in the ladder's order. The ladder itself is in `zTOC.md > ## Ladder`.

##### refactor: extract config loader opening

The cycle's setup commit: create the bookmark, delete `## Closed`'s contents, move the
Todo entry into this block, and bump the version-of-record.

##### refactor: split loader from parser

Loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load without parsing and a test cannot parse
without a file on disk.

* The two jobs share one function and one error type.
  - `config/loader.rs` finds and reads the file, returning the text and its path, so a caller that
    only wants to know which file was read stops here.
  - `config/parser.rs` takes text and returns the schema, so a test hands it a string and never
    touches the filesystem.
    - the error type stays shared for now, since splitting it would change the messages
      `config --validate` prints and the acceptance check compares them
* `main` still reaches into the parse result by field.
  - `main` calls `config::load` and receives the schema, so the field access moves behind the module
    boundary and the CLI no longer knows the file's shape.

##### refactor: extract config loader closing

Closing out the cycle.

- 1 (current) [refactor: split loader from parser](TODO.md#refactor-split-loader-from-parser)
- [refactor: extract config loader closing](TODO.md#refactor-extract-config-loader-closing)

    return textwrap.fill(x, 100, break_long_words=False, break_on_hyphens=False)

plan_solution = between("Provisional. Three steps, each doing one thing", "#### Acceptance check\n\nThis cycle's, pass")

delib = between("#### Deliberation\n\n- Close makes no agent commit", "- This cycle is local and work-only until its Land")
rungs = between("##### feat: the readers take any mix of ochid and ocid", "##### feat: test repos, vc-dr-apply, and the v0.3.1-(0,1,2) agent-files closing")

opening ([Cycle-record](AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).

  and the trial's own, stay.
- The `vc-dr-apply.sh` work done under review here went to the rung after, **feat: vc-dr-apply takes the active version and offers language skeletons**, and

  two local commits and no push or Land.

##### feat: vc-dr-apply takes the active version and offers language skeletons

older than the ones being tried, a script in `~/bin` found no skeletons, and a repo with no code had
no `[validate]` to start from. Split out of the rung before, wink's call (2026-11-04), since its
title described half of what it held. Agent-files `v0.3.1-2`, the draft the rung before began,
wink's call (2026-11-04).

  got `v0.3.0` from `main` and not the `v0.3.1-2` in use. Both repos now default
  to `@`, the working copy as on disk, jj snapshotting it first, `--landed` takes `main` for both,
  and the plan and the suggested body name a working copy by its change id. The `-2` rules say so:
  the Set, **Changing the agent-files**, its rationale, and the proposal's **New repos start from an
  adopter's rules**, renamed from "committed rules".

  first acquaint asked about `[validate]` in a repo with no code: `scripts/vc-dr-apply-lang/`
  holds `none`, the doc checks, `rust`, in `cargo new`'s shape, `c-cpp`, one choice for both, CMake
  with clang-tidy, a `format` target, and `ctest --no-tests=error`, and `python`, uv, ruff, and
  pytest. Each but `none` has one passing test where its runner fails on none, and replaces the
  base skeleton's `version.toml`, its build system holding the version. Its `validate.toml` is
  appended to `.vc-config.md`, refused when one is there, and a new language is a new directory,
  `--lang` alone listing them. `{module}`, `{name}` with `_` for `-`, fills Python's package path.
  Each was applied to a throwaway workspace and its full `validate` passed there, which found that
  clang-tidy enables no checks without a `.clang-tidy`, and the skeleton ships one.
- The skeletons come from the source, wink's (2026-11-04), so the script may live in `~/bin`:
  `scripts/vc-dr-apply-base/`, `work/` and `gitignore-lines`, and `scripts/vc-dr-apply-lang/`, one
  directory per language, named apart from the script and with no nested `lang/`. They are read
  from the source work repo at the revision in use, so they match the agent-files they come with,
  `--landed` included. `--skel DIR` takes them from a directory as on disk, and a source with none,
  as `main` is today, falls back to the script's own directory, symlinks resolved. `--lang` alone
  lists from SOURCE or `--skel`, and the plan names where the skeletons came from. Tried from a copy
  outside vc-x1, its C/C++ workspace validating, and through a symlink and a copy with `--landed`,
  the first falling back and the second refusing with `--skel` named.

  the uncommitted applied set into its cycle, or to commit the config alone when there is none.

  work having been reviewed whole before the split. The waiver covers the two local commits and no
  push or Land.

##### feat: the ladder lives in zTOC.md alone

The ladder was in two places, `TODO.md`'s list and `zTOC.md`'s, kept in step by hand, and zed's
preview follows only `zTOC.md`'s links, which go to another file, wink's finding (2026-11-04). The
list moves to `zTOC.md` alone, its markers with it, wink's call:

- `TODO.md`'s `#### Ladder` becomes `#### Rungs`, the subsections under it and a line pointing at
  `zTOC.md`, and the ladder's references `[0]` to `[19]` leave `TODO.md`'s `# References`, `[50]`
  staying.
